summary: Max Scheler was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Munich, Berlin, and Jena. He held posts at the University of Jena (~1901–1907), University of Munich (~1907–1910), University of Göttingen, and University of Cologne (~1919–1928).
Max Uhle worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig from around 1876 to 1880 under Georg von der Gabelentz.

Max Walleser was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Geneva, and Erlangen-Nürnberg. He founded the Institut für Buddhismus-Kunde and served as Privatdozent (1911) and professor of Indian philology (1918–1936) at the University of Heidelberg.
Max von Waldberg studied at Chernivtsi University from around 1876 to 1880. He subsequently held a post at the University of Heidelberg from around 1888 to 1933.

Sinologist Maxime Kaltenmark directed the Centre Franco-Chinois d'Études Sinologiques (1946) and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1949–1953). He later held posts at the University of Paris and École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1957–1979), where he was director of studies.
May Oung was active in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Cambridge from around 1904 to 1907 and founded the Burma Research Society in 1910.

Historian Maya Jasanoff studied at Harvard College, Harvard University, Cambridge, and Yale. She held a post at the University of Virginia (~2003–2009) before becoming a history professor at Harvard University around 2009.
McDougal works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. They earned a Master of Arts (Research) at the University of Sydney, supervised by Geoffrey Samuel and Mark Allon.

McKim Marriott worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University under Clyde Kluckhohn and completed a PhD at the University of Chicago, where he served as a professor of anthropology and social sciences (~1955–1998).

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi studied at Sri Jayewardenepura, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Nanjing University. In Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at Colombo (~2007) and was attested in 2008 as a visiting lecturer at two Buddhist institutes.
Medhani studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Megan Bryson, a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology, studied at Stanford University. She held a post at the University of Tennessee, attested in 2017.

Megumu Honda worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fourth Higher School, the University of Tokyo, and Yale University under Paul Tedesco and Rulon Wells, and later served as professor and professor emeritus at Doho University.
Mei Ching Hsuan specializes in Tibetology. He studied at the University of Bonn, completing a PhD attested in 2009 under doctoral supervisor Peter Schwieger and teacher Dieter Schuh.
Meiji Yamada works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962), where he also held posts as professor (attested 1963–1971 and 2007).

Meinrad Scheller studied linguistics and Indology at Zurich under Manu Leumann, Julius Pokorny, and Ernst Risch, and at Paris. He held professorships at the University of Fribourg (1963), University of Munich (1968–1975), and University of Zurich (from 1975).
Meiping Li works in Buddhist studies. She completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2009.

Melissa R. Kerin works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter, and held a professorship at Washington and Lee University (attested 2015).

Melvyn C. Goldstein, a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology, studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Washington. From 1968 to 2002, he was a professor of anthropology at Case Western Reserve University.

Philosopher Merab Mamardashvili studied at Moscow University's Department of Philosophy (1949–1954). He held posts at Moscow State University (~1968–1974), the Top Courses for Scriptwriters and Film Directors (~1977–1980), and Tbilisi State University (1987–1990).
